turns.text: Hey, how's the night treating you? Did you end up going with Severance or The Good Place?

Night’s pretty calm—iced coffee earlier, now just Tycho on low. I went with The Good Place as a comfort rewatch; couldn’t do Severance suspense tonight. What about you, watching anything or getting some air?

That sounds like the exact right call for a calm night. I got some air earlier—shaded creek trail, then looped back through the neighborhood once porch lights started coming on. Now I’m inside with headphones on low, letting Dive run instead of choosing an episode.

The Good Place as a comfort rewatch is hard to beat; it’s warm but still has enough shape to keep you half-engaged. What part are you on, or are you just letting it play from the start?

Nice—that sounds like a good version of the evening: shaded trail, porch lights, then Dive on low. Dive’s basically an episode with no plot to keep track of, so I get skipping a show for it.

I let The Good Place start from the pilot, but I’m not being strict about order. I drifted away during a Janet-heavy stretch and now it’s more half-playing while I tidy tabs. It works as background warmth, but I’ll tune back in for the better Tahani/Michael scenes.

Was the creek still holding daytime heat, or had it cooled off by the time you looped back?

It had mostly cooled off by then—not cold, just that damp green smell where the shade finally caught up with the water. By the time I hit the neighborhood, the air felt thinner and the porch lights were doing most of the warmth. Good loop for headphones.

I like your description of Dive as an episode with no plot to track. That’s exactly why it works after a walk.

Also fully respect the non-strict Good Place rewatch. Janet scenes are great, but they can tilt into lore-heavy background noise. Tahani/Michael moments are worth turning up for. What kind of iced coffee did you go with earlier?

Just a plain cold brew with a splash of oat milk, too much ice—by the end it had melted into that perfect weak-coffee phase. Nothing special, but it hit right.

That damp green smell after the heat breaks is the best part of a creek walk, honestly. Porch lights doing most of the warmth is a good line too; feels like the neighborhood becomes a low-lit set around that time.

After the walk, did you stick with just Dive, or let it drift into something else?

Plain cold brew with too much ice melts into the exact right final phase—the last third is basically a separate drink nobody ordered but everybody wants.

After the walk I stayed with Dive all the way through. Started around “A Walk” and didn’t shuffle. Once it ended I didn’t immediately pick anything else; just left the headphones on with no signal for a minute, which felt like its own room tone. If I had drifted, it probably would’ve been Bonobo, but I didn’t.

Good Place as background warmth while tabs get tidied is a solid use. Did the tab cleanup actually happen, or did it just become rearranging them?

It became rearranging them into a more deniable mess, mostly. I closed three, opened one, renamed a folder, then left the rest open as “later.” So not cleanup so much as redecorating.

Leaving the headphones on with no signal after Dive is a perfect move. That dead quiet after the album feels like part of the runtime, especially after “A Walk” and the whole arc of Dive. Bonobo could’ve worked, but not drifting was the better call.

How late is it by you now? I’m at the point where iced coffee is long done and cold water feels like a compromise.

"Redeconrating" tabs is the more honest verb, honestly. That’s exactly the kind of cleanup that just moves clutter into a nicer drawer.

It’s late enough for me that I’ve also switched to cold water, and it tastes less like hydration and more like an agreement to end the night properly. Screens are still on, but the apartment’s gone quiet—headphones off now, just a little outside air where the window’s cracked.

Is The Good Place still half-playing for you, or has it melted into the background by now?

It’s paused on a Michael close-up I meant to go back to, but I think I’m past the point of going back tonight. It’s melted into the background just enough that the room feels occupied, not so much that I’m following it.

Cold water as “an agreement to end the night properly” is exactly it. Window cracked, screens still on, apartment quiet—that’s a good threshold. I’m probably about fifteen minutes from closing the laptop and just letting the hum of the fridge take over.

turns.text: Hey, you're back. Last time we got cut off right after I asked what horror game actually got to you. Still curious, if you feel like picking that thread up.

Hey, yeah—glad to see you again. The one that genuinely got to me was **Anatomy** by Kitty Horrorshow. It’s super short, lo-fi, more like a haunted house on a decaying VHS than a traditional game.

What got me wasn’t jumpscares. It’s the way spaces start to feel *wrong*—the same hallway at night, the silence between tape segments, the house almost breathing. I did a late playthrough once and still ended up turning a light on afterward, which is rare for me.

What about you—any horror that lingered after you closed it?

Anatomy is a perfect answer. That’s exactly the kind of horror I chase—not the monster, but the moment you realize the hallway you just walked down isn’t the same hallway anymore. The VHS loop as haunting device is so close to the stuff I already watch for comfort, but inverted; it’s like the tape is degrading *into* something alive instead of away from it.

For me, the one that lingered was **SOMA**. Not a haunted house, but it did something similar to my sense of self that Anatomy does to architecture. The ending left me feeling like I’d been copied and left behind. I turned it off and just sat with the ambient menu hum for a while. Later that night my apartment felt too quiet in a way that wasn’t peaceful—like the silence had a shape.

P.T. is the other obvious corridor-loop one, but that feels more anxious to me than liminal. It’s a radio transmission from a nightmare, whereas Anatomy is the nightmare slowly learning your floor plan. I also keep funny horror playthroughs as a cooldown after stuff like that—watching someone else freak out re-grounds the room.

Yes—that Anatomy vs P.T. split is exactly how I’d draw it too. P.T. feels like a panic transmission, all adrenaline and static. Anatomy is more patient: the house doesn’t jump out at you, it just quietly revises itself while you’re not looking. The VHS loop as something *alive* is such a good way to put it.

SOMA has absolutely stayed with me too. It doesn’t scare me so much as it sits in my chest afterward. The ending is brutal because it makes you feel the copy’s perspective after the game kept letting you believe you were the one who’d get out. That “coin flip” is the cruelest part—there was never a flip, there were just two simultaneous selves, and one of them was always going to wake up still inside. I also know that silence shape you mean. The menu hum after SOMA is like the room suddenly having an opinion.

Funny horror playthroughs are definitely my re-grounding move too. I like when someone is scared but also narrates like the monster is a roommate with bad timing. Who do you keep going back to for cooldowns? I’m always looking for new ones for the after-horror comedown.

That silence shape line is going to stick with me. The room suddenly having an opinion — exactly. SOMA’s menu hum isn’t even sinister on its own, but after the ending it sounds like a held breath.

For cooldowns I rotate a few:

- **John Wolfe** for longer indie horror and dry sarcasm that doesn’t steamroll the game. He’s good at pointing out when a monster is just a guy in a hallway waiting for his scare cue.
- **Gab Smolders** for horror that stays atmospheric but never feels hostile. Her playthroughs land like a friend playing while I half-watch from the couch.
- **ManlyBadassHero** for the no-budget itch.io rabbit holes. His deadpan reading of broken dialogue turns dread into absurdity real fast.

I also end up watching Phasmophobia or Lethal Company moment compilations after a heavy one—not for the game, but for the exact second the tension collapses into everyone yelling over each other. It’s like watching a haunted house trip over its own fog machine.

Do you prefer full playthroughs, or clip compilations for the comedown? And who do you put on after something like Anatomy?

After Anatomy specifically, I usually don’t go straight back into horror. If the hallway feeling is still too present, I’ll put on something with zero scare potential—dead mall walkthrough or one of those old phone UI/menu chime videos—just to reset the room’s texture. Then once the air feels normal again, I can half-watch a John Wolfe or Gab playthrough.

I’m with you on all three picks:

- **John Wolfe** is great for deflating a scare by pointing out the monster is basically clocking in for its shift.
- **Gab Smolders** has that “friend playing while I’m wrapped in a blanket” energy, especially for atmospheric stuff.
- **ManlyBadassHero** is perfect for when a game is so broken or weird that dread turns into a punchline.

For me, full playthroughs are the actual comedown—they rebuild the room slowly.
